newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Difficult year ahead for Central Asia-Red Cross.
newsitem.headline: Difficult year ahead for Central Asia-Red Cross.

text.p: War, hunger and the collapse in social welfare in the five former Soviet republics of Central Asia prompted a $21 million appeal by the International Federation of the Red Cross on Monday.
"We have cases of malnourishment in Kazakhstan," Bob McKerrow, the agency's representative in the region, told a news conference in Almaty, the Kazakh capital.

He said children in western Kazakhstan, a region whose entire harvest was destroyed by drought this year and which is also prey to acute environmental problems, were often only eating one meal a day of just bread and tea.
McKerrow said the agency lacked figures to show the exact extent of the problem but there were alarmingly high rates of anaemia among feeding mothers.
The agency also viewed the upsurge in fighting in Tajikistan's four-year-old civil war with concern. "We're preparing for the worst," McKerrow said.

He said the refugee crisis from Afghanistan threatened to spill over into Turkmenistan. Fighting in western Afghanistan had already forced several hundred people to seek shelter across the border in Turkmenistan.

McKerrow said the appeal for 1997 was double that of 1996 and would comprise mostly supplementary food aid to combat malnutrition. The Central Asian republics, along with those of the war-torn Caucasus, have been hardest hit by the collapse of the Soviet Union.
